# Diamond Prajna Paramita Sutra <note>The Diamond Sutra</note>

<note>original: 金剛般若波羅蜜經</note>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the four stages of enlightenment and whether a practitioner who has attained them would cling to the concept of having achieved a specific rank or fruit.</meta>

Form, sound, smell, taste, touch, and mental objects <note>referring to the six sense objects or spheres</note>; this is why one is called a <term>Srota-apanna</term> <gloss>Stream-enterer</gloss>.
"What do you think? Does a <term>Sakridagamin</term> <gloss>Once-returner</gloss> have this thought: 'I have attained the fruit of a Once-returner'?"
Subhuti replied, "No, World-Honored One. Why? Because although a <term>Sakridagamin</term> is named a 'Once-returner,' in reality there is no such thing as going or coming. Therefore, he is named a <term>Sakridagamin</term>."
"Subhuti, what do you think? Does an <term>Anagamin</term> <gloss>Non-returner</gloss> have this thought: 'I have attained the fruit of a Non-returner'?"
Subhuti replied, "No, World-Honored One. Why? Because an <term>Anagamin</term> is named a 'Non-returner,' but in reality there is no such thing as not coming. For this reason, he is named an <term>Anagamin</term>."

<summary>This page discusses the second and third stages of Buddhist sainthood, explaining that those who attain these levels do not perceive themselves as possessing a fixed status or identity. The text emphasizes that true enlightenment involves transcending the labels of coming and going.</summary>
<keywords>Subhuti, Sakridagamin, Anagamin, Diamond Sutra, emptiness, enlightenment, non-attachment, Once-returner, Non-returner</keywords>
